text_blocks.snippet: High blood pressure (hypertension) is often called a "silent killer" because it typically causes no signs or symptoms at all.
snippet_highlighted_words: no signs or symptoms at all

list.snippet: No warning signs: Most people with high blood pressure feel completely normal and do not realize their pressure is high.
The only way to know: Measuring your blood pressure with a cuff monitor is the only reliable way to detect the condition.

text_blocks.snippet: When blood pressure spikes to dangerously high levels (above 180/120 mm Hg), it can cause a medical emergency. Call 911 immediately if you have a reading over 180/120 combined with any of these critical symptoms:

list.snippet: Shortness of breath or difficulty breathing
Sudden, severe back or abdominal pain

text_blocks.snippet: While not reliable early warnings, some individuals experiencing severely elevated blood pressure or rapid spikes may notice:
Learn more about monitoring guidelines and risk factors from the American Heart Association, review detailed explanations at the Cleveland Clinic, or check official health guidance via the CDC.
